name: pdk-verdaccio-shared-s3-dynamodb-storage
instr:
# Shared Verdaccio storage

We need to run two or more Verdaccio registries without a shared filesystem. Add an in-repository `aws-storage` plugin and wire it into Verdaccio's storage configuration so a configured bucket and table provide one registry: S3 holds package manifests and tarballs; DynamoDB holds the package index, manifest revisions and npm tokens. The plugin is selected by `store.aws-storage` with `bucket`, `table` and `endpoint` properties. Put it at `packages/plugins/aws-storage` as the package `verdaccio-aws-storage`, built with Vite like `packages/plugins/local-storage`, using the `@aws-sdk` v3 clients. Each manifest revision is written as a new S3 object whose key contains `snapshots`. Registries without this setting continue to use local storage.

- A package published through either registry is immediately readable through the other, and its tarball can be downloaded there.
- Concurrent publishes of distinct versions of the same package both succeed, including when creating the package; neither version is lost. Concurrent publishes of an identical version yield one success and one HTTP 409.
- With the shared plugin, a single-version unpublish is the npm client's `PUT /<package>/-rev/<revision>` carrying the manifest without that version and with no attachments, which Verdaccio currently rejects as an unsupported registry call. Such a revision-protected unpublish concurrent with a dist-tag update never resurrects a removed version or discards the tag or ano
